historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 12, Page 163 The name Yaeesh carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Yaeesh ibn Amr Al-Kindi (d. 662 AD) was the founder of the Umayyad Dynasty in Damascus, which ruled the Islamic Empire from 661 to 750 AD. He was also known as Muawiyyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and is considered the first Umayyad caliph. Yaeesh is mentioned in this historical account as a powerful military commander and a prominent figure during the early Islamic period.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri's Ansab Al-Ashraf, Volume 4, Page 366 The name Yaeesh carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Yaeesh ibn Abd al-Malik (d. 724 AD) was the sixth Umayyad caliph and the son of Caliph Abd al-Malik. He is also known as Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik. During his reign, he continued the construction of the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, which was initiated by his father. Yaeesh is mentioned in this historical account as a patron of Islamic art and architecture.
